the co-ocurring trajectory of maternal substance use and psychological maltreatment, and how it is associated with the development of children's problem behaviors.
the co-occurrence of substance use and parenting behaviors, specifically psychological control, and their effects on child behavioral outcomes.

the EBFT intervention is effective in reducing substance use and psychological aggression among mothers and that these changes are associated with reductions in child behavior problems.
EBFT has a positive effect on the trajectory of substance use and psychological parenting control in mothers and that this effect is associated with a reduction in children's problem behaviors.

the results from this study suggest that the EBFT is a promising intervention that can improve the quality of parenting among substance using mothers and, consequently, the behavior problems of their children.

the family systems therapy, Ecologically Based Family Therapy, is a viable treatment for substance use disorders and that it can also help to improve parenting behaviors, which in turn improves child behavioral outcomes.
